selected.title: Five baby orangutans found in India raise questions about wildlife trafficking
selected.summary: Villagers in India found five baby orangutans in a forest in September. Their discovery has brought fresh attention to the illegal wildlife trade and to questions about how endangered animals are moved across borders.
selected.why_it_matters: A single discovery can expose how wildlife trafficking connects distant places—and put pressure on authorities to trace animals’ origins.
selected.challenge_question: Where were the five baby orangutans found?
selected.answer_explanation: The villagers first spotted the five orangutans in a casuarina forest in India. Their unexpected presence raised questions about illegal wildlife trade.
selected.butterfly_question: What should happen when an endangered animal is found far from its natural home?
